Stability statistics of a multi-environment trial

Source: R/breeding.R
stability.Rd

Parametric and rank-based stability statistics computed from the table of genotype means in every environment and the pooled error of the trial:

"eberhart"

Eberhart and Russell (1966): regression coefficient b on the environmental index (with its standard error from the genotype's own deviations, and a t test of b = 1), deviation mean square s2d (mean scale, minus the error of a mean) with its F test against the pooled error, and their analysis of variance.

"finlay"

Finlay and Wilkinson (1963): regression on the environment mean, optionally on the log scale.

"shukla"

Shukla's (1972) stability variance sigma2 and the same after removing the linear regression on the environmental index (s2), with F tests against the pooled error (plot scale).

"wricke"

Wricke's (1962) ecovalence (plot scale) and its share of the interaction.

"kang"

Kang's (1993) yield-stability statistic YS: the rank of the mean (highest = g), adjusted by the LSD, plus the stability rating from Shukla's test (-8, -4, -2 at 0.01, 0.05, 0.10).

"huehn"

Huehn's (1979) rank statistics S1 and S2 on the ranks corrected for the genotype effects, with the Z tests of Nassar and Huehn (1987).

The common analysis of variance follows Shukla (1972): the interaction is split into the heterogeneity of the regressions and the residual, with (g - 1)(e - 2) degrees of freedom (Eberhart and Russell printed g(e - 2), but e - 2 of them belong to environments and are identically zero).

Usage

stability(
  data,
  response,
  genotype,
  environment,
  block = NULL,
  mse = NULL,
  df_error = NULL,
  reps = 1,
  method = c("eberhart", "finlay", "shukla", "wricke", "kang", "huehn"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  log_finlay = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

genotype, environment

Names of the genotype and environment columns.

block

Optional name of the block (replicate) column; blocks are taken as nested within environments.

mse, df_error

Error mean square (plot scale) and its degrees of freedom, only when the data hold one mean per cell.

reps

Number of replicates behind each mean, when the data hold one mean per cell.

method

One or more of "eberhart", "finlay", "shukla", "wricke", "kang" and "huehn" (default: all).

alpha

Significance level of the LSD in Kang's statistic and of the critical values of Huehn's tests.

log_finlay

Fit the regression of Finlay and Wilkinson on the natural logarithm of the means, as in their paper.

Value

An object of class "ad_stability": the analysis of variance (anova) and one element per method.

References

Eberhart, S. A. and Russell, W. A. (1966) Crop Science 6, 36-40. Finlay, K. W. and Wilkinson, G. N. (1963) Australian Journal of Agricultural Research 14, 742-754. Shukla, G. K. (1972) Heredity 29, 237-245. Wricke, G. (1962) Zeitschrift fur Pflanzenzuchtung 47, 92-96. Kang, M. S. (1993) Agronomy Journal 85, 754-757. Huehn, M. (1979) EDV in Medizin und Biologie 10, 112-117. Nassar, R. and Huehn, M. (1987) Biometrics 43, 45-53.

Examples

st <- stability(maize_met, "Yield_t_ha", "Hybrid", "Environment", block = "Block")
st
